120245250941310138.summary: The review-led ad showed real ring photos and customer proof, but its 1.72% link CTR was well below the 4.05% account average.

why.point: The social proof was clear.
why.evidence: The image leads with “Rated 4.8/5 with 500+ verified reviews” and shows 2 named reviewers with 5 stars and quotes.

why.point: The product was visible on hands.
why.evidence: The image shows 2 close-ups of rings being worn, including a colourful stone ring and a gold ring.

why.point: Click interest was weak.
why.evidence: Link CTR was 1.72%, below the 4.05% account average, across 276,571 impressions.

why.point: Sales efficiency cannot be judged.
why.evidence: Purchases, purchase value, ROAS and CPA are missing. Account averages are 3.75 ROAS and INR 9,387.08 CPA.

structure.layout: Collage with review panels and ring photos on hands.
structure.product: Rings shown worn in 2 close-up photos.
structure.text_on_image: Rating, reviewer names, stars, customer quotes, Order Now, and 7-day easy return and lifetime exchange.
structure.proof: 2 named customer reviews with 5 stars, plus a 4.8/5 rating and 500+ verified reviews.
structure.cta: Order Now on the image; Shop Now as the ad button.
structure.look: Plum, yellow and cream blocks with close-up hand photos and large review text.

keep: Lead with the 4.8/5 rating and 500+ reviews.
Show rings being worn, not only product shots.
Keep specific customer feedback about fit, quality and service.
Keep the return and exchange reassurance visible.
test_next: Use 1 short review and 1 larger ring photo to reduce clutter.
Test a first-frame hook focused on fast ring resizing.
Test a video showing the ring on hand with the customer quote as captions.
Test a single review about craftsmanship against one about service.
watch_out: The image has dense review text that may be hard to read on mobile.
The 1.72% link CTR is well below the account average.
Purchases and ROAS are missing, so sales impact is unknown.

120239698169900138.summary: The ad drew strong clicks and beat the account average CPA, but its ROAS was slightly below average and it made only 3 purchases.

why.point: The April birthday hook was timely and direct.
why.evidence: The image says “APRIL BIRTHSTONE” and the copy frames diamonds as a better birthday gift than a gift card.

why.point: The product was easy to see in context.
why.evidence: A close-up shows a model wearing a small dangling floral earring, though the jewellery itself appears small.

why.point: The ad attracted clicks.
why.evidence: Link CTR was 12.77%, well above the 4.07% account average.

why.point: Efficiency was mixed.
why.evidence: CPA was ₹6,997.33, better than the ₹9,628.39 average, but ROAS was 3.06 versus the 3.41 average.

why.point: The purchase result is based on a small sample.
why.evidence: The ad spent ₹20,991.99 across 16 days and recorded 3 purchases.

structure.hook: “APRIL BIRTHSTONE” with “April birthdays deserve Diamonds, not gift cards.”
structure.layout: Close-up portrait fills most of the image. Headline and supporting line sit near the bottom, with a shop button below. Offer and product range banners sit at the top and bottom.
structure.product: Small dangling floral earring worn on the model’s ear.
structure.text_on_image: “APRIL BIRTHSTONE”; “April birthdays deserve Diamonds, not gift cards.”; “SHOP GEHNA”; “Free shipping ✦ Lifetime exchange”; “NATURAL AND LAB GROWN DIAMONDS AVAILABLE.”
structure.offer: Free shipping and lifetime exchange are shown on the image. Copy also mentions free shipping.
structure.proof: Image footer says natural and lab-grown diamonds are available. Copy claims 18K BIS hallmarked gold and natural diamonds.
structure.cta: SHOP GEHNA button on image; SHOP_NOW ad button.
structure.look: Premium beauty portrait with a dark background, white text and a maroon banner.

keep: The April birthday gifting angle.
The close-up view of the earring being worn.
The clear free shipping and lifetime exchange message.
The natural diamond and 18K gold claims in the copy.
test_next: Show the earring larger so its design is easier to inspect.
Test a product-only image beside the model image.
Test copy that leads with natural diamonds and 18K gold instead of the gift-card comparison.
Make the natural and lab-grown options clearer so the image and copy do not seem to conflict.
Compare the April-specific message with an evergreen gifting version.
watch_out: The earring is small in the image, which may limit product understanding after the click.
The image mentions lab-grown diamonds while the copy focuses on natural diamonds.
Only 3 purchases make the ROAS result uncertain.

120237466537150138.summary: Strong click and sales efficiency beat account averages, but only 2 purchases make the result uncertain.

why.point: The ad drew more clicks than average.

why.point: Sales efficiency was strong but based on few purchases.

structure.proof: 4.8/5 Google Reviews rating, 5 stars, and a named customer quote.
structure.look: Muted blurred background, cream review card, orange stars, and purple customer name.

keep: Use a visible customer review and star rating.
Keep the offer and end date clear in the ad copy.
Show the jewellery product alongside the review.
Keep the 14K and 18K gold detail in the copy.
test_next: Make the jewellery larger while keeping the review card.
Test a shorter customer quote with the same rating.
Add the 15% offer to the image.
Test a close-up product image against the current layout.
watch_out: Only 2 purchases make the high ROAS and low CPA uncertain.
The product is small and the image does not show the sale offer.

120235364793920138.summary: The ad drew above-average clicks and ROAS, but its high CPA and only 3 purchases make the result mixed.

why.point: The image makes the pearl chain easy to notice.
why.evidence: A close-up of a woman wearing the necklace shows its shape and how it looks on a person.

why.point: The creative earned more clicks than average.
why.evidence: Link CTR was 4.93%, above the 4.07% account average.

why.point: The reported return was strong, but purchases were costly.
why.evidence: ROAS was 6.38 versus 3.22 average, while CPA was ₹21,079 versus ₹9,289 average, from 3 purchases.

why.point: The image and copy give clear quality cues.
why.evidence: The image says BIS hallmarked, natural gemstones and lifetime exchange. The copy adds 18K gold and natural gemstones.

structure.hook: Top banner: BIS hallmarked, natural gemstones, lifetime exchange.
structure.layout: Close-up portrait with the product name in a box at the right. A banner sits at the top and a tagline at the bottom.
structure.product: A woman wearing a luminous baroque pearl chain, with a small gold earring also visible.
structure.text_on_image: 18K Gold Chain, Luminous Baroque Pearl, and “Imperfect symmetry shaped by the sea into effortless elegance.”
structure.offer: No price or discount. Lifetime exchange is stated.
structure.proof: BIS hallmarked and natural gemstones are stated on the image. The copy also says the chain is 18K gold.
structure.cta: Shop Now in the ad. None on the image.
structure.look: Polished, close-up jewellery styling with a soft, natural background.

keep: Show the necklace on a person so shoppers can judge its scale and wear.
Keep the pearl detail and the simple product name.
Keep the BIS hallmark and lifetime exchange claims easy to see.
Keep the short, elegant product story.
test_next: Show a full-length view of the necklace against a plain background.
Test a macro image that makes the baroque pearl shapes clearer.
Make the product name larger and move it away from the necklace.
Test copy focused only on the pearl chain, without mentioning Navratna.
Test a version with the product price or a clear value cue.
watch_out: CPA is more than 2 times the account average, despite the strong ROAS.
Only 3 purchases support the result, so performance may be uneven.
The image shows pearls while the copy also mentions Navratna, which may make the product story less focused.

120246163414290138.summary: This ad beat account averages on all 3 key metrics, though results came from only 2 purchases.

why.point: The deadline made the sale feel urgent.
why.evidence: The image says “DAY LEFT” and “DON’T MISS IT”; the copy says the sale ends tomorrow.

why.point: The offer was clear and easy to notice.

why.point: The jewellery had a clear visual focus.
why.evidence: A hand holds a fine chain with a white teardrop pendant against a simple background.

why.point: The results were well above account averages.
why.evidence: ROAS was 12.57 vs 3.77, CPA was ₹4,850 vs ₹9,317, and link CTR was 7.94% vs 4.03%.

structure.layout: Centered sale message above a large jewellery image, with a bottom callout
structure.product: Fine chain with a white teardrop pendant, held by a hand
structure.text_on_image: Gehna, End of Season Sale, EOSS, up to 15% off, dates, DAY LEFT, and DON’T MISS IT
structure.cta: “DON’T MISS IT” on the image; SHOP_NOW in the ad
structure.look: Minimal pale background with black text, gold accents, and a burgundy callout

keep: Keep the clear sale deadline.
Keep the discount prominent.
Keep a close product image against a simple background.
Keep the direct SHOP_NOW action.
test_next: Test “1 DAY LEFT” on the image instead of “DAY LEFT.”
Test a close-up of the pendant on a person to show scale.
Test a version that names 18K gold and natural gemstones on the image.
Test a shorter copy version with the deadline and discount in the first line.
watch_out: Only 2 purchases came from ₹9,700 spend, so the high ROAS may not hold at scale.
The image shows a single necklace, while the copy promotes a mixed jewellery range.
